caption: my human tried to lose me 37 times 🐺
logline: A dog tells how its human tried to lose it thirty-seven times, and why he never once made it sit.
question: why tf would he try to lose his own dog?
premise: The narrator is Buh's tamed wolf, said openly from line 1. Buh (16, never named aloud) has tried to lose it 37 times: tamed wolves teleport back to their owner from 12 blocks, unless they're sitting, and a sitting dog waits forever. He wants it to forget him, so he never makes it sit. He keeps talking about college; every night he says sorry.
twist: He was leaving the game for good and wanted the dog free, not waiting. On the last morning he walks it up Dog Hill to his old hut, says 'sit, boy' and 'I'll be right back', and the chat says 'Buh left the game': the one sit he avoided 37 times is the one he finally used. The first frame of Dog on the Hill.

lines.text: My HUMAN / has TRIED / to LOSE me / thirty-seven TIMES.
He RUNS. / I FOLLOW. / Twelve BLOCKS out, / I just APPEAR / right NEXT / to HIM.
He HID / in the WHEAT. / He tried HILLS / at NIGHT. / He SWAM / to an ISLAND. / I POPPED up / on the BEACH.
The ONLY time / I DON'T / POP up / next to HIM / is WHEN / I'm SITTING.
He KNOWS that. / A SITTING dog / waits FOREVER. / He WANTS me / to FORGET him. / So he NEVER / makes me SIT.
He keeps TALKING / about a PLACE / called COLLEGE.
Every NIGHT / he SAYS, / SORRY, buddy. / I don't KNOW / what FOR.
Last NIGHT, / a ZOMBIE / came for HIM. / I got THERE / FIRST, though.
This MORNING, / he WALKED me / BACK home, / up the HILL / to his HUT.
He SAID, / I'll BE / right BACK.
